mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% over the prior 8 weeks reduces expected equity discount rates, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for at least 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified rate hike period (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound exceeding 2% in the next month indicates a turning point in supply-side demand shocks, which tends to precede a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market interprets the recovery as a bottom.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months then rises more than 2% in the third month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window following the identified bottom signal (IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months suggests a cooling demand environment, lowering growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior month's (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the RSAFS exceeds 10% in a single month, it indicates a large surprise in money supply growth, which often precedes a sharp move in equities as investors anticipate future policy responses.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no significant reaction (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500K for two consecutive months, in the context of falling unemployment, creates a dual labor and housing demand signal that is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1500 and UNRATE < 4.0 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: resuming housing market expansion with strong labor conditions
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically significant relative to the signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS increasing and UNRATE rising), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be negative over the next 20 days as higher discount rates erode future earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS up trend and UNRATE up trend
failure_condition: During the identified regime, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (IC > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 2% each month for three months suggests a dual supply shock, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates further contraction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO down 2% or more for three months AND CPIAUCSL down 2% or more for three months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (IC > -0.15).
